title: Smart Thermostat Rebates in Windsor 2026: $125 Back
desc: Windsor smart thermostat rebate for 2026: $125 from Home Renovation Savings, Enwin Utilities as distributor, and Peak Perks for central air.
lead: Windsor has the mildest winters on the list apart from Niagara Falls, a January low of -6.2°C, and 72% of its 94,275 households live in a house type the $125 rebate covers.
cards_heading: What Ontario pays for a smart thermostat in Windsor
cards_intro: We re-read the three program pages on October 4, 2026. The rebate is province-wide, so the amount is the same in every city, and the page that matters is the one that says whether your home and heating qualify.

cards.title: Smart thermostat
cards.note: One rebate on an eligible smart thermostat, claimed with a code at checkout or with a receipt uploaded within 60 days of buying.

cards.title: Who is eligible
cards.amount: Gas heat or electric heat or cooling
cards.note: You must be an Enbridge Gas customer heating mainly with a gas furnace or boiler, or be on the Ontario grid and use electric heat or cooling, and live in a house, semi, row, townhome or mobile home on a permanent foundation.

cards.title: One per household, ever
cards.note: A smart thermostat rebate, discount or free device from Enbridge, Save on Energy or Home Renovation Savings in the past rules you out.

cards.title: Peak Perks
cards.note: A prepaid card for joining the summer demand response program with central air or a heat pump controlled by an eligible Wi-Fi thermostat.

cards.title: Energy Affordability Program
cards.note: Households under the income limits get a programmable or smart thermostat, depending on the home, with other upgrades at no charge.

cards.title: Cornwall excluded
cards.note: Cornwall Electric customers cannot join the rebate or Peak Perks.

after_cards: The rebate page states no end date, so confirm it is still open before you buy.
sections: With a January low of -6.2°C, Windsor's winters are not harsh, so central air is a bigger part of a household's year than in the north. That makes Peak Perks, which needs central air and an eligible Wi-Fi thermostat, worth a look. It pays $75 on enrollment and $20 a year.

Enwin Utilities supplies electricity, and Windsor postal codes begin with N, which the Energy Affordability Program lists. 37% of households rent. 60% live in detached homes and 13% in buildings of five or more storeys.

The program pays for single detached, semi-detached, row, townhome and mobile homes on a permanent foundation. In Windsor about 72% of 94,275 households live in one of those. If yours is an apartment or a duplex unit, this rebate is not written for you, and the Energy Affordability Program is the route to ask about.

Before you buy, press the program page's Get code button, receive a code by email and enter it at checkout on the Home Depot, Best Buy, Copeland Sensi, ecobee or Mysa website. After you buy, press Apply for rebate and upload the receipt within 60 days. Either way the thermostat has to be one of the listed models, and a Windsor homeowner who buys in a store should keep the receipt.

The rebate page does not say owners only. It asks that you live in an eligible home type and that either gas or electric heating or cooling applies. In Windsor, 37% of households rent. A tenant should still get the landlord's agreement before replacing the thermostat on the wall and should ask whether it goes back when they leave.
claim_steps: Check that your home type, heating and cooling match the eligibility card, and that you have not had a thermostat offer before.
Pick one of the listed models from ecobee, Google Nest, Honeywell Home, Copeland Sensi, Mysa or Sinopé.
Get a code from the program page and use it at checkout, or buy first and upload the receipt within 60 days.
If you have central air, enroll the same thermostat in Peak Perks. Enwin Utilities is your local distributor, but Peak Perks is run by Save on Energy.
If your household income is under the program limits, call 1-844-770-3148 before buying, since a free thermostat may be available.
faq: Does Enwin run a thermostat rebate?
We did not find one on the pages we read.
Can I do Peak Perks with a heat pump?
Yes, if it is part of central air and an eligible thermostat controls it.
Do I need to own my home in Windsor?
The page does not say owners only.
Through the Energy Affordability Program, if income is under the limit.
